answer:
RESULT.

HYPOTHESIS (natural-language characterisation of MN and SG via PC1 of forms of capital):

On a single global PCA of the twelve Z forms of capital across all 39 hundred-year slices of capital.csv (BCE 4300..500), PC1 captures 30.3 % of the variance (eigenvalue 3.64; |corr(PC1, cross-sectional mean Z)| = 0.53). When oriented so that positive PC1 corresponds to a co-intensification of social prestige objects (ZCU_AU copper-and-gold +0.41), pottery decoration (Zkeverz +0.38), depot hoards (ZHort +0.34), hatchets and swords (ZAxtSchwert +0.30), daggers (ZDolch +0.27), monument size (ZMW +0.24), house size (Zhausgr +0.23) and monument count (ZMonument +0.20) — i.e. a positive pole dominated by economic+social+symbolic capital together with cultural decoration — and the negative pole dominated by pottery-form standards (ZKeform -0.35), the axes-and-celts economy (ZBeil -0.24), amber (Zamber -0.24) and sickles (ZSichel -0.15), the two phases look as follows.

The Middle Neolithic (MN, BCE 3400..3000, n = 5) sat at mean PC1 = -1.374 (SD 0.489) — the lowest integrated position in the sequence — with a within-phase linear trend of slope = -0.259 per 100 yr going forward in time (raw slope vs BCE +0.0026, R² = 0.699, p = 0.078), so PC1 kept falling through the second half of the fourth millennium BCE. In raw Z terms MN was the phase in which pottery-form standards (ZKeform mean +0.71), axes-and-celt abundance (ZBeil +1.08), amber (Zamber +0.51), monument count (ZMonument +0.47) and house-size (Zhausgr +0.29) were *high*, while copper-and-gold (ZCU_AU -0.43), depot hoards (ZHort -0.44), hatchets-and-swords (ZAxtSchwert -0.41), daggers (ZDolch -0.47), pottery-decoration (Zkeverz -0.50) and monument-size (ZMW -0.06) were *low* — i.e. an economic-and-raw-material-rich / weapons-and-prestige-poor configuration that, in the global axis, projects to a strongly negative PC1. Sickles (ZSichel) were constant at 0 in all five MN slices and contribute no within-phase information.

The Younger Neolithic (here encoded as 'SG' / Single-Grave in capital.csv, BCE 2900..2300, n = 7) lay partially recovered at mean PC1 = -1.117 (SD 0.430), with a within-phase linear trend of slope = +0.120 per 100 yr going forward (raw slope vs BCE -0.0012, R² = 0.363, p = 0.152), driven by the BCE-2700 MonumentCount peak (+3.95 Z), the rebound of depot presence from BCE 2800 onward and the late BCE-2300 spike in daggers (ZDolch -0.58 -> +0.80). On the global axis SG is *above* MN by SG-mean minus MN-mean = +0.257 (Welch t = +0.94, p = 0.374; Mann-Whitney U = 24, p = 0.343) — the direction is consistent across all twelve adjacent slices but the difference is not significant at this sample size. Daggers in SG are essentially flat at -0.58 for six of seven slices, contributing almost no within-phase information.

PC1 is also strongly positively correlated with the Belau pollen openness PC1 at 100-yr smoothing (r = +0.73, p < 10^-6, n = 36) and with pollen_inter_100 (r = +0.48, p = 0.003, n = 37) over the whole window, so the SG recovery on PC1 sits on a backdrop of *stabilising* landscape openness: within-MN PC1 rises with openness (r ≈ +0.65 to +0.73), within-SG it is roughly flat or slightly inverse (r ≈ -0.21 to +0.21). Pollen_acc-rate is uncorrelated with PC1 (r = +0.02, p = 0.90), so the hypothesis should not lean on a demographic driver.

Three limitations are recorded explicitly. First, the 100-yr transition window 3000..2900 BCE has no slice in capital.csv; the Brasskamp / Endneolithikum horizon is therefore invisible to the PCA and is interpolated only by the linear trends of MN and SG. Second, ZSichel is exactly 0 in all five MN slices and ZDolch is constant at -0.58 in six of seven SG slices — these variables carry no phase-discriminative information but participate in shaping the global axis. Third, the MN-below-SG ordering depends on the global standardisation anchored to the EN and LN/YBA tails of the 4300..500 BCE range: re-running PCA restricted to 3400..2300 BCE flips six of twelve loadings and reverses the MN/SG sign (SG-mean - MN-mean = -3.70), even though the within-MN downward trend is preserved qualitatively. The point estimate of the phase difference is therefore not robust to the choice of standardisation window, although the *direction* of MN-as-trough-of-integrated-capital and SG-as-partial-recovery rests on the same global PCA axis.

In summary, MN was characterised on PC1 by a strongly negative position (mean PC1 -1.37) and a continued within-phase decline (slope -0.26 / 100 yr forward, R² 0.70, p 0.08), with the leading positive-side forms of capital — copper-and-gold, pottery-decoration, depot, hatchets-and-swords, daggers, monument-size, house-size, monument-count — all weak, while pottery-form, axes-and-celt, amber and sickle stayed elevated. SG was characterised by a less negative mean PC1 (-1.11) and a within-phase rise (slope +0.12 / 100 yr forward, R² 0.36, p 0.15), with monument count, depots and late daggers at BCE 2300 providing the recovery; the same positive-side capital forms partially re-assert themselves on the global axis, against a backdrop of stable rather than increasing landscape openness.

WORKFLOW:
  1. Loaded capital.csv (comma-encoded decimals), time_series_data.csv, pollen_openness_score_Belau_Woserin_Feeser_et_al_2019.csv from data/.
  2. Built 39 x 12 matrix of raw Z columns from capital.csv (centred BCE 4300..500 in 100-yr steps; 12 capital columns, no missing values; constant MN ZSichel noted).
  3. Re-standardised each column over the full 4300..500 BCE window and ran PCA on the 12 x 12 correlation matrix (numpy.linalg.eigh).
  4. Oriented PC1 sign so that positive PC1 correlates positively with the cross-sectional mean of the 12 standardised Zs (|corr| = 0.534); orientation was flipped once and recorded.
  5. Computed per-slice PC1 scores and split into phases using query masks: MN (BCE 3400..3000, n = 5) and SG (BCE 2900..2300, n = 7). The 3000..2900 BCE gap is empty.
  6. Per phase: mean PC1 and SD; scipy.stats.linregress of PC1 vs BCE giving raw slope, slope per 100 yr forward (i.e. -100 x raw slope), p-value and R²; counted within- and across-phase statistics (Welch t, Mann-Whitney U) for SG - MN.
  7. Sorted PC1 loadings by absolute magnitude; reported per Bourdieu category (symbolic ZAxtSchwert/ZDolch/Zhausgr, social ZCU_AU/Zamber/ZMonument, cultural ZKeform/Zkeverz, economic ZHort/ZSichel/ZBeil/ZMW).
  8. Sensitivity: re-fit PCA on the truncated 3400..2300 BCE window only (12 columns, 15 slices), re-standardised within that window, re-applied the same orientation rule, and compared loadings' signs vs the fit on the full window along with the SG-mean - MN-mean difference (sign_changed_by_truncation = true; reported).
  9. Overlaid pollen proxies: Belau_PC1 SMOOTH_MEAN_100y from the openness file at -BCE matching per slice, and pollen_inter_100 / pollen_grate_100 from time_series_data.csv at the same offset; computed Pearson r with PC1 over the full window and within MN and SG.
 10. Limitations recorded: 3000..2900 BCE gap, near-constant ZSichel and ZDolch, sensitivity of MN/SG ordering to standardisation window.
